en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Great Chapter 4:
The Question on the Infinite Body (Anantakāya)
Then it occurred to King Milinda:
"This bhikkhu is wise and capable of conversing with me;
there are many points that I ought to ask about, yet before those points have been asked, the sun will [set]."
"It will lead to our welfare; what if I were to converse with him tomorrow in the inner palace?
Then the king said this to Devamantiya:
"In that case, Devamantiya, you should inform the venerable one: 'Tomorrow there will be a conversation with the king in the inner palace.'"
Having said this, King Milinda rose from his seat, took leave of the Elder Nāgasena, mounted his chariot, and departed, reciting the words “Nāgasena, Nāgasena.
Then Devamantiya said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“Venerable sir, King Milinda says this:”
“There will be a discussion with the king within his own inner palace.
“Very well,” the Elder consented.
Then, at the end of that night, Devamantiya, Anantakāya, Maṅkura, and Sabbadinna approached King Milinda; having approached, they spoke thus to King Milinda:
“Let the venerable Nāgasena come, Great King.
“Yes, let him come.
“With how many bhikkhus shall he come?”
“Let him come with as many bhikkhus as he wishes.
Then Sabbadinna said,
“Let him come, Great King, together with ten bhikkhus.”
A second time the king said,
“Let him come with as many bhikkhus as he wishes.
A second time Sabbadinna said:
“Let him come, Great King, together with ten bhikkhus.
A third time the king said:
“Let him come together with as many bhikkhus as he wishes.”
A third time, Sabbadinna said:
“Let him come, Great King, together with ten bhikkhus.
“But all this hospitality has been prepared; I am saying, ‘Let him come with as many bhikkhus as he desires.’”
"Tell me, this Sabbadinna speaks otherwise; why is it that we are not capable of providing food for the bhikkhus?
When this was said, Sabbadinna became dejected.
Then Devamantiya, Anantakāya, and Maṅkura approached the Venerable Nāgasena; having approached, they spoke thus to the Venerable Nāgasena:
“Venerable sir, King Milinda says this:
‘Let him come with as many bhikkhus as he wishes.
Then, in the morning, the Venerable Nāgasena dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāgala together with eighty thousand bhikkhus.
Then Anantakāya, walking along supporting himself on the Venerable Nāgasena, said this to the Venerable Nāgasena:
"Venerable Nāgasena, as for this which you call 'Nāgasena,' what here is the Nāgasena?
The Elder replied:
“But who, in this case, do you consider to be ‘Nāgasena’?
“Venerable sir, it is that internal wind, the life-force, which enters and exits, that I consider to be ‘Nāgasena.
“But if this wind were not to exit after having entered, or enter after having exited, would that man live?”
“No, venerable sir.
“But when these conch-blowers blow their conches, does the wind enter back into them?
“No, venerable sir.”
“But as for those bamboo-blowers who blow their bamboos, does the wind enter them again?
“No, venerable sir.
“But as for those horn-blowers who blow their horns, does the wind enter them again?”
“No, venerable sir.
“Then why do they not die?
“I am not capable of conversing with such a debater as you; it would be well, venerable sir, if you would state the meaning yourself.”
“This is not the soul; these inhalations and exhalations are merely bodily formations,” the Elder spoke this discourse on the Abhidhamma.
Then the lay follower Anantakāya declared himself a follower.
Thus ends the fourth inquiry concerning Anantakāya.
